fullPassage:
Multisensory experiences are a central part of our everyday lives, yet we often take them for granted, especially when our senses function normally or are corrected to normal with aids like glasses.

(A) And it does not stop there. Even the sounds that come both from the atmospheres in which we eat and our interactions with the food (such as chewing) and the tools we use to eat influence our eating experience.

(B) However, closer inspection to any, even the most ordinary experiences, reveals the remarkable multisensory world in which we live. Consider the experience of eating a regular meal.

(C) At first, it may seem like an ordinary experience, but it is actually a fusion of the senses. We first eat with our eyes, but we are also exposed to countless sensory signals that influence our eating experience such as food textures, tastes, and smells.

questions.passage: (A) And it does not stop there. Multisensory experiences are a central part of our everyday lives, yet we often take them for granted. However, closer inspection to any, even the most ordinary experiences, ①<u>reveals</u> the remarkable multisensory world. At first, it may seem like an ordinary experience, but it is actually a ②<u>fusing</u> of the senses. We first eat with our ③<u>eyes</u>, but we are also exposed to countless sensory signals such as food ④<u>textures</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① fusing → fusion: '감각의 결합'에서 관사 a 뒤에 명사가 필요. fusing은 동명사/현재분사이므로 명사 fusion이 적절
✅ ② reveals: 단수 주어 inspection에 3인칭 단수 동사 일치
✅ ③ eyes: 복수 명사 정상
✅ ④ textures: 복수 명사 정상
det.tip: a + 명사: a fusion(○) / a fusing(×). fusion = 융합(명사)

questions.passage: (A) And it does not stop there. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① correcting → corrected: 감각이 '교정되는' 것(수동)이므로 과거분사 corrected. are corrected to normal(수동태)
✅ ② function: 자동사 정상
✅ ③ exposed: be exposed to(수동) 정상
✅ ④ that: signals를 선행사로 한 주격 관계대명사 정상
det.tip: are corrected(수동) = 교정되다. are correcting(능동진행) = 교정하고 있다

questions.passage: Multisensory experiences are a central part of our everyday lives, yet we often take them for granted, especially when our senses function normally or are corrected to normal with aids like glasses. (A) And it does not stop there. (B) However, closer inspection to any, even the most ordinary experiences, reveals the remarkable multisensory world in which we live. Consider the experience of eating a regular meal. Even the sounds ①<u>that</u> come both from the atmospheres ②<u>in which</u> we eat and our interactions with the food (such as chewing) and the tools ③<u>we use to eat</u> ④<u>influences</u> our eating experience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④(관계대명사) ②~에서 ③우리가 먹기 위해 사용하는 ①영향을 미치다(→influence)
det.analysis:
❌ ① influences → influence: 주어가 'the sounds'(복수)이므로 복수 동사 influence가 맞음. 중간의 수식어구가 길어 주어를 놓치기 쉬움
✅ ④ that: sounds를 선행사로 한 주격 관계대명사 정상
✅ ② in which: 전치사+관계대명사(= where) 정상
✅ ③ we use to eat: 목적격 관계대명사 생략 + to부정사 정상
det.tip: 주어-동사 수 일치: the sounds(복수) → influence. 긴 수식어 사이 주어 찾기

✅ ③①④ 원문 일치
det.tip: few(적은)↔countless(수많은). 다감각 경험 = 수많은 감각 신호

det.analysis: ✅ take for granted: 원문 'we often take them for granted'
det.tip: take for granted = 당연시하다

questions.passage:
Multisensory experiences are a central part of our everyday lives, yet we often take them for granted, especially when our senses function normally or are corrected to normal with aids like glasses.

(A) And it does not stop there. Even the sounds that come both from the atmospheres in which we eat and our interactions with the food (such as chewing) and the tools we use to eat influence our eating experience.

(B) However, closer inspection to any, even the most ordinary experiences, reveals the remarkable multisensory world in which we live. Consider the experience of eating a regular meal.

(C) At first, it may seem like an ordinary experience, but it is actually a fusion of the senses. We first eat with our eyes, but we are also exposed to countless sensory signals that influence our eating experience such as food textures, tastes, and smells.
